no, the ISP only sees you are going to a Tor entry guard

you -> ISP -> tor entry guard -> middle node -> exit node -> destination

  • you know who you are and where you are going
  • ISP knows who you are and that you are using Tor
  • Entry guard knows who you are (IP address only) but not where you are going
  • Middle node does not know who you are or where you are going
  • Exit node does not know who you are but knows where you are going.
  • Destination does not know who you are and thinks you came from exit node

this assumes you have not done anything to identify your self such as log into an account you have logged into with out Tor or logged into a site over http

I finished reading recently "Homer and Langley" by E.L. Doctorow.

It is more of a novella told by the blind narrator Homer Colyer about his life as an eccentric hoarder living with his brother, Langley, on Fifth Avenue in Harlem. The events of the story take place roughly between the first world War and Vietnam.

Doctorow based the story on the lives of two real life eccentric brothers, known as the "Colyer brothers" who were notorious hoarders. At one point, Langley battles the bank that holds their mortgage, and the Con Edison company about their electricity. Langley is a compulsive collector, going so far as to bring an old Ford Model T into the living room of their brownstone mansion in a failed attempt at restoring it. The brothers also have a few interesting encounters with a gangster named Vincent.

It is good historical fiction, set entirely in Manhattan, and a very quick but enjoyable read.
